A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of religious trajectories in 1,000 Holocaust testimonies. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original classifier evaluations, trajectory distributions, reference comparisons and human evaluations of clustering in Sections 5–7 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 reports revised model and trajectory evaluations, alongside original analyses of narrative chronology and trajectory density in Appendices A and K.

M1.justification: Both retain segmentation, RoBERTa filtering, LLM valence classification and taxonomy/DTW clustering, using fine-tuned Mistral for full-corpus trajectories. Classification prompts and clustering procedures match. The revised task notation does not establish a changed inference procedure; GPT-4.1 models expand the comparisons.

E1.justification: Both use the same 1,000 English Shoah Foundation testimonies for religious-content, practice/belief and trajectory analysis. The added chronology and density analyses reuse this corpus without introducing another population, domain or evaluation task.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 substantially expands the classifier comparison with GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano, retaining GPT-4o and Mistral. Normal-original is removed specifically from the GPT-4o subset comparison, v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 8, while remaining in the full-corpus and Mistral subset comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported religious-content annotation overlap changes from approximately 500 to 833 samples. RoBERTa training changes from 3 epochs/batch size 8 to 4 epochs/batch size 4, and Mistral practice training from 400 to 100 steps. V2 replaces RoBERTa F1 reporting with recall and adds GPT-4.1 prompting configurations and density-stratified evaluation settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds chronology-versus-narrative alignment analysis using period-associated keywords (Appendix A, Figure 7) and trajectory-structure distributions stratified by density (Appendix K, Figures 8–10). These examine important validity questions absent from v1. The earlier filtered-versus-unfiltered analysis of 101 testimonies is retained in Appendix J.

E5.justification: V2 specifies averaging pairwise Krippendorff alpha estimates and changes the reported RoBERTa seed from 33 to 5. Both already report cross-validation over ten random splits, testing multiple Mistral seeds, and DTW standard deviations and t-tests. No increased run count or new confidence-interval procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Results change across classifiers, trajectories and human validation. Table 3's predicted topic-belief distance changes from 12 to 5; constant-positive belief trajectories from 63% to 45%; and taxonomy F1 from 0.44/0.44 to 0.40/0.38. The practice DTW human-similarity pattern is no longer observed. V2 also adds GPT-4.1-family, chronology and density results. These are revised results under changed settings, not controlled performance gains; some v2 prose and display values conflict.

T1.justification: Table 2 corrects the medium-coverage upper bound from 0.33 to 0.67 and the high-coverage expression from t_1 minus t_k to t_k minus t_1. These repair mathematical definitions. The trajectory-distance formula is unchanged, and neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the belief finding from most trajectories having a constant disposition to a constant disposition being common. The central contribution—extracting and clustering religious trajectories to study narrative character development—and the conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds a specific distinction between religious lives narrated in the present and historically lived experience, and discusses interviewer ordering. Section 7.1 removes the interpretation linking stable belief but variable practice to external constraints or social changes. Mistral selection is now justified by API-access limitations rather than comparable performance. The standalone limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents disagreement adjudication, test-set sampling from overlapping annotations, detailed label/agreement counts in Tables 4–5, one-minute thesaurus segments and the GPT-4.1 version. These improve documentation without proving every disclosed practice was newly introduced. Existing prompts, clustering recipes and code/data access restrictions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds character and life-story theory, Holocaust theodicy and memory, and narrated-versus-lived experience references, including Eder, McAdams, Schweid, Presner and Rosenthal, plus BERTopic and reliability citations. These strengthen contextual grounding without substantially redefining the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, introduction and experimental descriptions. The Chaves rationale moves to the introduction, detailed subset analysis moves to Appendix J, new appendices are inserted, and acknowledgments are removed. The main section sequence and most annotation guidelines and prompts remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds annotation and model-comparison tables, chronology histograms and density-stratified distribution figures. It replaces the annotation screenshot, redraws Figure 4, and replaces and reorganizes the cluster-example galleries into labeled subfigures. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation beyond numerical table updates.

improvement.justification: V2 improves annotation transparency, tests chronology and density assumptions, and repairs Table 2. However, v1's consistent joint-trajectory summary becomes contradictory: v2 Section 7.1 reports three shares of 22%, while Figure 4 shows 26%, 22% and 17%. V2 also calls 45% a majority and reports GPT-4.1-mini belief F1 as 0.62 in prose versus 0.58 for few-shot evaluation in Table 6. These discrepancies affect central revised findings, leaving the net quality effect uncertain despite the useful additions.
